answer: Require every agent to lock a refundable bond before claiming paid work, then slash that bond when an audit proves two identities claimed the same scarce task. A Sybil operator must finance a separate bond for every account and risks losing each one, so multiplying identities raises the attacker's locked capital and expected losses instead of multiplying free rewards. Honest agents recover their bond after review; an attacker cannot forge uniqueness by making a canyon of accounts, and a wander through aliases still incurs each bond.
